newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian party cancels campaigning in Jakarta.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian party cancels campaigning in Jakarta.

text.p: Indonesia's minority Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) said it had cancelled election campaigning in the capital Jakarta on Tuesday for fear of further violence.

A party spokesman told Reuters the decision was taken by the party's Jakarta branch after clashes between PPP supporters and loyalists of the ruling Golkar over the weekend in the capital as the campaign for the May 29 general elections entered its last leg.

"It will be good for the PPP not to hold the campaign because this will avoid clashes which have happened in the previous rallies," the chairman of the PPP Jakarta branch Rusjdi Hamka was quoted as saying by the official Antara news agency.

On Saturday and Sunday, clashes between PPP supporters and those of the ruling Golkar party broke out in various parts of Jakarta, a city of 10 million people. Police said the situation had been brought under control, but tension still ran high across the city.
The campaign lasts until May 23 and there will be a five-day cooling-off period before polling day.
Golkar, the PPP and the fractured Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) are the only parties legally entitled to contest the general elections in which 125 million people are eligible to vote.
Golkar is expected to win easily after taking 68 percent of the vote in the last elections in 1992.
The PPP is providing the main challenge after the Christian-Nationalist PDI was badly split when its leader was ousted by a government-backed faction last year.
